subject: Dedicated capacity sizing clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Torres <a.torres@fintechx.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: sizing details from today's demo

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it was helpful. I promised I'd send the quick traffic summary so you can fine-tune the dedicated sizing recommendation. High-level context: production goes live in Q3; we need options for predictable monthly cost but also headroom for marketing-driven spikes.

Attached: sample-prompt-traffic.csv (30k rows — time, endpoint, avg_tokens, max_tokens). Important datapoints from our side:
- Steady-state TPS (text gen): ~350 TPS across weekday business hours
- Burst peak (marketing events): ~1,200 TPS sustained for 15-30 minutes, occasional 2-3 minute micro-spikes to ~1,800 TPS
- Token mix: avg request = 256 tokens; 75% text generation/instruction completions, 20% short chat-ish sessions, 5% embeddings/reranking at ~512 tokens
- Typical max sequence length seen: 1,024 tokens for long-form generation tests

Questions we want answers to from Redwood:
1) Given the above, which GPU flavor would you recommend as the baseline for Dedicated (H100 vs A100 80GB vs L40s)?
2) What concurrency per GPU do you expect for our token mix (estimates of effective user-level concurrency and batch sizes)?
3) How should we plan capacity for burst traffic — do you recommend burst-only spare pool or autoscale policy with warm standby?
4) Any quick ideas on cost-down levers (quantization, smaller model variants) that are conservative on quality loss?

Also, procurement will want a simple SKU-level estimate and timeline — copying them on follow-ups. Looking to schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the workbook you send.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
VP Product, FinTechX

--

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: sizing details from today's demo

Alex — really helpful data, thank you. I ran a quick pass and attached a first-draft capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx that models three scenarios (conservative, balanced, aggressive). High-level notes below; workbook has the line-item math and cost delta table.

Top-level recommendation (balanced):
- Baseline: 4x H100 80GB (driver + 3 workers) configured for continuous batching and KV cache; this covers ~350 sustained TPS with p95 latency within your 300–500 ms SLO for avg 256-token requests.
- Burst handling: add a 4-GPU warm standby (same GPU flavor) that can be spun to full capacity within ~90s; for marketing events we recommend autoscale with fast-shift policy + transient pre-warm for scheduled campaigns. This gives headroom to ~1,400 TPS.
- Peak micro-spikes: For the ~1,800 TPS micro-spikes, mixing in cheaper L40s as overflow is possible if you accept slightly higher p95 and/or use a smaller model variant for non-critical requests.

GPU flavor tradeoffs:
- H100: best raw throughput + memory for long sequences + best KV cache behavior for chat workloads (recommended if long-form quality is key).
- A100 80GB: close competitor; slightly cheaper per-hour but needs more instances to match H100 throughput for very high concurrency patterns.
- L40s: cost-effective for inference-heavy, shorter sequence workloads or scaled-out overflow pools; not ideal if you need 1K+ tokens with low latency.

Concurrency / batching assumptions in the workbook:
- Effective per-GPU concurrency for your mix (avg 256 tokens): H100 ~110-150 concurrent in-flight requests (with continuous batching set to 20–60ms threshold).
- Batch sizes: typical effective batch size ~64–128 tokens per micro-batch depending on sequence length distribution.

Cost-down levers we modeled:
- Aggressive quantization (int8) for a non-critical subset (e.g., embeddings / rerank) can cut token compute by ~35% with small quality delta.
- Serving a distilled/smaller model for ephemeral marketing flows can reduce burst cost while preserving primary model quality for critical paths.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat user flows offers 10–25% token savings depending on cache hit rate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether KMS/HSM key separation is required for this workspace (Monica — can you confirm FinTechX's policy?).
2) Rachel/Ben to finalize the SKU-level estimate in the workbook and return a one-page cost vs latency summary for procurement.
3) 30-min follow-up demo next Tue/Thu to walk the workbook and pick preferred GPU flavor + autoscale policy.

I've attached: capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx and a short call recording. Happy to iterate once you confirm KMS/requirements.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--

Quick add from our side — two operational clarifications before we finalize SKUs:
- If FinTechX requires Private (VPC) deployment, the autoscale warm-standby timeline increases (networking and customer IP allowlist steps add ~2–3 business days to warm-up). That affects how aggressive we make the warm standby vs hot pool decision.
- For KMS/HSM: we can integrate customer KMS but there is an onboarding checklist (certs + key rotation policy) — Monica, happy to hand this to you to confirm with Alex's procurement.

Also looping a short note: we should propose an H100 baseline in the one-pager, and include an optional A100 line-item as a lower-cost alternative with recommended instance counts.

Ben

Thanks Rachel and Ben — very clear and helpful. A couple quick confirmations:
- KMS is a hard requirement (we use a centralized HSM-backed key for all secrets). Monica will coordinate certs and the onboarding checklist.
- We prefer H100 baseline if it keeps latency predictable for long-form generation; include A100 as the optional cost-saving alternative in the one-pager for execs.
- For bursts: we'll plan scheduled pre-warms for marketing campaigns (we control the schedule) and want autoscale for unpredictable spikes. Please model both in the SKU estimate.

Procurement: can you confirm expected lead times for issuing a PO? We want to line up approvals once we have the one-page cost/latency summary.

Next step: Rachel — can you send the updated one-pager (H100 baseline + A100 optional line + autoscale/warm-standby assumptions) by Monday EOD? If so, we'll lock a 30-minute slot next Tue to run through final numbers and get a verbal go/no-go from our engineering lead.

Appreciate it — Alex
VP Product, FinTechX
